stem: A platform team is deciding, separately, which CloudWatch-based metric should drive a worker fleet's scale-out when its real bottleneck is a growing backlog rather than CPU, and whether that fleet's instance type is already right-sized. Which TWO choices are correct? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: A target tracking policy on ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible
A target tracking policy on network in/out
AWS Compute Optimizer's analysis of the fleet and its Auto Scaling group

rationale: A target tracking policy on ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible ties scale-out directly to the queue backlog, matching a bottleneck that is a growing backlog rather than CPU. Compute Optimizer's analysis of the fleet and its Auto Scaling group is what answers whether the instance type is already right-sized, based on historical CloudWatch data. CPU-utilization target tracking scales on how busy instances already are, which the scenario says is not the real bottleneck here. A predictive scaling schedule forecasts and pre-scales for a recurring load pattern; it does not target a backlog metric or address rightsizing at all. Network in/out target tracking reflects data transfer volume, not the number of queued jobs waiting to be processed.
